question: What the original does with the lend-lease IC share when the country has no lend-lease receiver: forced, locked, skipped, and where; what happens to the share the last receiver leaves; what the screen shows.

addresses.name: CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit
addresses.comment:
**Every frame the production screen is open, before the sliders are balanced, each slider standing above its limit is put down to it.** rva 0x3FE06C..0x3FE10A of CProductionView::Update, unconditional within it (no branch from earlier in Update lands past it). For each slider of the view's list (+0xB8) in list order - upgrade, reinforcement, supply, production, consumer goods, lend-lease:

    lim = slider->setting (+0x34)->slot 11()          ; GetNoLimit -1.0 for five, CDistributeLendLease::GetLimit for lend-lease
    if (lim >= 0 && GetValue(slider) > lim)            ; fcompi: jb skips lim < 0, jbe skips value <= lim
        CProductionView::AddToSlider(slider@ESI, (float)(GetValue(slider) - lim))

The amount is the excess, positive, so AddToSlider's raising arm caps it and the slider ends at min(TotalIC, lim). **So with no lend-lease receiver (GetLimit 0.0) the lend-lease slider is held at 0, and with receivers at the cap TotalIC x GetMaxLendLeaseFraction** - also while the player drags it, since nothing here asks IsHeld. Two gaps, both AddToSlider's: an excess under 0.005 IC rounds to nothing and is left, and a disabled (locked) slider is not touched. The value set latches the scrollbar's moved byte (CEconomySlider::SetValue passes markMoved = 1), so the balancing rounds that follow count the slider as held, share what it gave up among the free ones and mark sliders_changed (+0x324) - the clamp reaches the model through SendDistribution within a wall-clock second. Only the played country's screen runs it: the simulation, the AI and the Lua clamp nothing. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7FE06C..0x7FE10A from the loop head: esi = [list node], [esi+0x34] -> [ecx] -> call [edx+0x2c] (slot 11), fldz/fxch/fcompi/jb 0x7FE108 (skip lim < 0); GetValue 0x7F0C30 into [esp+0x80], slot 11 again, fld [esp+0x80]; fcompi; jbe 0x7FE108 (skip value <= lim); GetValue again, slot 11 again, fsubr qword [esp+0x88] = value - lim, push, call 0x7FEBD0 with esi the slider. A scan of Update's jumps (disasm 0x7FD350..0x7FDFC0, every j* target in 0x7FExxxx/0x7FFxxxx) found none past 0x7FE06C, so the block is not skipped. GetLimit 0x518BD0 read whole. Wrong if a jump into 0x7FE110 from elsewhere in Update exists that the scan missed, or if slot 11 at table offset 0x2C were not GetLimit for CDistributeLendLease (vtable.py --holding 0x518BD0: CDistributeLendLease slot 11 only).

addresses.name: CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders
addresses.comment:
**The rounds that keep the six IC sliders summing to TotalIC.** rva 0x3FE114..0x3FE38F of CProductionView::Update, straight after CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit; up to ten rounds ([esp+0x58]):

    left = GetMaximum(first slider)                     ; TotalIC
    free = the list's count (+0xC0)
    for each slider s, list order (index i):
        CEconomySlider::Update(s); CEconomySlider::LatchMoved(s)
        left -= GetValue(s)
        if (IsDisabled(s) || IsHeld(s) || view->+0x320 > 0) free--
        country->+0x1090[i] = IsDisabled(s)          ; where i is inside that vector
        sliders_changed (+0x324) |= (s->pinned (+0x3E) || IsHeld(s)); s->pinned = 0
    step = left / free
    if (|left| > 0.005) { if (|step| < 0.01f) step = step < 0 ? -0.01f : 0.01f }  else step = 0
    if (free > 0)
        for each slider s, list order:
            if (left != 0 && !IsHeld(s)) left -= CProductionView::AddToSlider(s, step)
            if (|left| < 0.005) break
            s->moved (+0x3C) = 0
    if (step == 0) stop

So what is left is shared out in **equal amounts**, not in proportion, over the sliders neither locked nor latched as moved; each stays within 0..TotalIC and, for lend-lease, under GetLimit. A slider the screen set itself in one round is latched (CEconomySlider::SetValue marks the scrollbar moved) and so counts as held in the next. Nothing in it tests lend-lease or a receiver: the lend-lease slider's only special treatment is its slot 11 limit, through AddToSlider and the clamp before. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md and FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7FE114..0x7FE395: GetMaximum 0x7F0D90 of [[view+0xB8]] into [esp+0x54], [view+0xC0] into [esp+0x80]; per slider call 0x7F0290 then 0x7F1320, subsd GetValue; IsDisabled 0x7F10D0 / IsHeld 0x7F1170 / cmp [view+0x320] then dec [esp+0x80]; [country+0x1090][edi*4] = setne(IsDisabled); [esi+0x3E] read and cleared, or'ed with IsHeld into [view+0x324]. Step: divsd by free; comisd |left| against 0.005 (double at 0x160AAE8); comiss 0.01f (0x160A378), -0.01f (0x160A518). Second pass: ucomiss left vs 0 / IsHeld / call 0x7FEBD0 / subsd; break on 0.005 > |left|; mov [esi+0x3c], bl. Round counter cmp 0xA, jl 0x7FE114, skipped when step == 0. Constants read off the image. Wrong if the parity-flag tests (lahf; test ah,0x44; jnp) were misread - they jump on ordered equality.

addresses.name: CProductionView::AddToSlider
addresses.no_signature: the slider arrives in ESI, the amount is a float at stack:4 (ret 4) and the result comes back in XMM0 - both callers read it with cvtss2sd xmm0, xmm0 straight after the call (0x7FE323) - a whole-program convention no ordinary prototype expresses; the view is not an argument at all
addresses.comment:
**Adds an amount to one slider, read whole 2026-11-12** (revised from inferred). Callers CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit (0x7FE103) and CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders (0x7FE318); CTechnologyView has its own copy without the limit at 0x41C7E0. Floats through doubles:

    a = (int)(|amount| * 100 + 0.5) / 100, the sign put back   ; to the hundredth, so |amount| < 0.005 is nothing
    if (IsDisabled(slider)) return 0                        ; a locked slider takes and gives nothing
    if (a < 0)
        if (GetValue + a > 0) { SetValue(GetValue + a); return a }
        r = GetValue - 0.0; SetValue(0.0); return r         ; positive - see below
    if (a > 0)
        cap = GetMaximum(slider)                            ; TotalIC
        lim = slider->setting (+0x34)->slot 11()
        if (lim >= 0 && cap > lim) cap = lim                ; lend-lease: CDistributeLendLease::GetLimit
        if (cap - GetValue - a > 0) { SetValue(GetValue + a); return a }
        r = cap - GetValue; SetValue(cap); return r         ; negative where the slider stood above cap
    return a                                                ; 0: nothing set

**A limit of nought or more caps the raising arm**, so a lend-lease slider whose GetLimit is 0 (no receiver) can be given nothing and, if it stood above 0, is set to 0. **The lowering arm's overflow returns the slider's whole value with the wrong sign**: a slider taken from 0.3 to the floor by a step of -0.5 reports +0.3 added, not -0.3, so the caller's running `left` moves the wrong way for the rest of that round (the next round counts it again from the values). The floor is the literal 0.0 (0x160A270), not a define. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7FEBD0..0x7FEDC4 (int3 to 0x7FEDD0): andpd with 0x160A2C0 (abs mask), mulsd/divsd 100.0 (0x160A358), addsd 0.5 (0x160A308), cvttsd2si, mulsd -1.0 (0x160A368) for the sign; push esi; call 0x7F10D0 (IsDisabled) -> xorps xmm0 and ret 4; negative arm GetValue 0x7F0C30, subsd 0.0 (0x160A270), compare with 0.0f (0x15BED10); overflow at 0x7FECCE stores GetValue - 0.0 at [ebp+8] and SetValue(0.0) at 0x7FEDB7, returning [ebp+8]; positive arm GetMaximum 0x7F0D90, slot 11 ([edx+0x2c]) three times with fcompi against 0 and against the maximum. ESI is the slider at both call sites (mov esi,[edi] at 0x7FE080 and 0x7FE2E7). What changed: the slider register (ESI, was 'not traced'), the sign slip, the hundredth dead band, and confidence. Wrong if 0x160A270 were not the double 0.0 (read as 0.0 from the image).

addresses.name: CDistributeLendLease::GetLimit
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of CDistributeLendLease: the lend-lease slider's limit in whole IC, a float. **0.0 when the country's lendlease_distributions (+0x6B8..+0x6BC) holds no 16-byte entry** (`test end - begin, 0xFFFFFFF0; jle`) - no test of an entry's weight or effectiveness, of a convoy, or of whether the receiver can be reached, so a receiver at effectiveness 0 counts. Otherwise TotalIC (+0x604) * 1000 * CCountry::GetMaxLendLeaseFraction / 1000 (64-bit, truncated) over 1000.0 - the cap. **Not a marker only - corrected 2026-11-12**: CEconomySlider::Update shows the `limit` icon only for an answer above nought, so it is hidden with no receiver; but CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit puts the slider down to any answer of nought or more every frame the production screen is open, and CProductionView::AddToSlider will not raise it past one - **so with no receiver the player's lend-lease slider is held at 0, and with receivers at this cap.** The simulation never reads it: the daily share loop and CChangeInvestmentCommand::Execute clamp nothing. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x518BD0..0x518C42: [ecx+0x18] the country, [+0x6BC]-[+0x6B8] tested with 0xFFFFFFF0, jle to the arm that loads 0; else imul TotalIC by 0x3E8, imul by *GetMaxLendLeaseFraction(0x508A90), __alldiv by 1000 (0xB99980), fild / fdiv 1000.0 (0x160A300). The two readers of slot 11 that act on it are 0x7FE08D/0x7FE0BC/0x7FE0EE (the clamp) and 0x7FED0D.. (AddToSlider). What changed: the 'marker only' sentence, which was false. Wrong if those two call sites did not reach CDistributeLendLease's table (the setting at slider +0x34 is the country's ProductionDistribution entry, CProductionView::BuildSliders).

addresses.name: CCountry::GetMaxLendLeaseFraction
addresses.comment: **The lend-lease cap as a share of IC**, thousandths: 0 with no lend-lease target (lendlease_distributions +0x6B8 empty); else with n = EffectiveNeutrality (+0xA90) * 1000 / LEND_LEASE_NEUTRALITY_LIMIT (+0x100) - the limit taken as 10 (floor(10.5f)) where it is 0 - clamped to 0..1000: **LEND_LEASE_MAX_IC_LOW + (LEND_LEASE_MAX_IC_HIGH - LEND_LEASE_MAX_IC_LOW) * (1000 - n) / 1000**. TFH: 0.05 to 0.90, so a country at neutrality 0 may give 90% and one at 60 or more 5%. Registered to Lua under this name. Callers: CCountry::GetMaxLendLease and CDistributeLendLease::GetLimit. **The simulation never clamps the lend-lease share to it** (corrected 2026-11-12: this said the engine never did) - but through GetLimit it is the production screen's cap on the player's lend-lease slider (CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit), besides the marker, and it is the AI script's target. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Body not re-read beyond its head (0x508A90..0x508ADA: the same 0xFFFFFFF0 test on +0x6BC - +0x6B8, then GetDefines and +0x100/+0x104/+0x108 of the block at +0xBC). The correction is to the last sentence only, from the clamp at 0x7FE06C. Wrong if the clamp did not run for the lend-lease slider - it would then still hold of the screen.

addresses.name: CProductionView::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 6 of CProductionView: fills the screen**, every frame it is open (CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView calls the open view's slot 6). When the played country is not the one at +0x334 it rebuilds the trade list and the sliders first. Then: the seven resources through SetGoodsText - energy 5, metal 4, rm 6, oil 3, fuel 1, supplies 0, money 2; `nukes_value` from +0x90 with two decimals; `ic_value` as TotalIC, a plain integer; **`transports_value` and `escorts_value`** as the integers +0xB0 and +0xB4 followed by ' (+N)' when N is not nought, where N sums, over the country's Constructions (+0xF40) whose slot 15 answers yes, the line's size (+0x40) times `CONVOY_CONSTRUCTION_SIZE / 1000` (the define at [defines + 0x9C] + 0x34, divided first and truncated - 10 in Their Finest Hour), into escorts where the line's +0x58 is set and transports otherwise; the `escort` button disabled unless the technology status's +0x80 (`allow_escorts`) is set - **the `convoy` button is never touched**; **every building with `capital = yes` has a button looked up by the building's own key** and enabled or disabled by building_available; the sliders' maximum reset to TotalIC when it changed; **every slider above its setting's slot 11 limit put down to it (CProductionView_Update_ClampSlidersToLimit) - the lend-lease slider to 0 while the country gives lend-lease to nobody, and to its cap while it does**; the six sliders kept adding up to TotalIC over up to ten rounds (CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders), with SendDistribution at most once a wall-clock second; and the four lists - build_queue, ai_need_queue, trade_list, convoy_queue - rebuilt when their length differs from the model's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 4, FINDINGS-convoylines.md, section B, and FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Comment extended only: the maximum reset (0x7FE009..0x7FE06A, SetMaximum 0x7F0EB0 on every slider where (float)TotalIC differs from +0xC8) and the clamp (0x7FE06C..0x7FE10A) were not in it, and they sit between the building buttons and the balancing. Everything else in the old comment is kept word for word. Wrong if the clamp were reachable only on a path the frame does not take - no jump past it was found in Update.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::SetValue
addresses.comment: Sets the slider: hands the scrollbar `actual_slider`'s value object at +0x48 `floor((value + 0.0005) * 1000)` through its slot 7, CScrollbar_SetValue, **with markMoved = 1 and notify = 1**, and keeps the float at +0x38. So every value a view sets itself - ResetFromSetting, the clamp to a limit, a balancing step - latches the scrollbar's +0x252 exactly as a player's move does, which LatchMoved turns into the slider's `moved` (+0x3C) and IsHeld then answers for. `ret 8`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7F0CC0..0x7F0D78: push 1; push 1; push ecx then [edi] = the thousandths from 0x401FD0/0xC08870; call [[esi+0x48]+0x1C] - slot 7 of the table at +0x48, which the scrollbar constructor 0xA9DBBD sets to 0x15FF858, whose slot 7 is 0xA9F2B0. What changed: the two flags and what they cause. Wrong if 0xA9F2B0 did not pass its second argument to CScrollbar_MoveBy's markMoved (it pushes [ebp+0xC] there, and MoveBy writes +0x252 = 1 on [ebp+0xC] != 0 at 0xAA0150).

addresses.name: CScrollbar_SetValue
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CScrollbar_SetValue(void* valueObject@ECX, int value@stack:4, bool markMoved@stack:8, bool notify@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 of the scrollbar's value object at +0x48** (table 0x15FF858, which no RTTI class owns, so the name carries none): sets the value to `value` thousandths. current = floor((object +0x1D8, i.e. the scrollbar's value +0x220, + 0.0005) * 1000); CScrollbar_MoveBy(the scrollbar = ECX - 0x48, value - current, markMoved, notify); then puts the knob at +0x50/+0x54 of the object from 0xA9E810, by +0x1F4 and +0x23C. `ret 0xC`. CEconomySlider::SetValue calls it with markMoved = 1 and notify = 1, so a value the production or technology screen sets itself latches +0x252 like a player's move. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-lendleaseslider.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xA9F2B0..0xA9F3E0 (ret 0xC, int3 after; retsBefore empty): edi = ecx; [edi+0x1D8] + 0.0005 (0x160A460) times 1000.0, 0x401FD0/0xC08870; pushes [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], then the slot [esp] = [ebp+8] - current; esi = edi - 0x48; eax = esi; call 0xAA0060 (CScrollbar_MoveBy, scrollbar in EAX). The table 0x15FF858 is written at scrollbar +0x48 by 0xA9DBBD; slot 7 read from the image. vtable.py --holding 0xA9F2B0: no RTTI table. Wrong if MoveBy's second stack argument were not the one that sets +0x252 (it is [ebp+0xC], tested at 0xAA0127).

struct_fields.name: moved
struct_fields.comment: The scrollbar's +0x252 as LatchMoved found it: the slider was moved since the last look - by the player, **or by CEconomySlider::SetValue, which passes markMoved = 1** (corrected 2026-11-12: this said the player only). IsHeld answers yes while it is set, so a slider a view set itself in one balancing round counts as held in the next, and CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders or's it into sliders_changed (+0x324) - which is how a clamp to a limit gets sent. Cleared by the balancing's second pass.
struct_fields.evidence: LatchMoved 0x7F1320 (record) moves 'actual_slider''s +0x252 here; SetValue 0x7F0CC0 reaches MoveBy with [ebp+0xC] = 1, which writes +0x252 = 1 at 0xAA0150; IsHeld 0x7F1170 opens cmp byte [esi+0x3c], 0. Name and type unchanged; the comment's 'the player moved' was too narrow.

struct_fields.name: moved_latch
struct_fields.comment: Set to 1 by CScrollbar_MoveBy where its markMoved argument is set - a player's press or drag, and every CEconomySlider::SetValue through CScrollbar_SetValue; read and cleared by CEconomySlider::LatchMoved (into the slider's +0x3C) and by CLendLeaseDistribution::AnySliderMoved.
struct_fields.evidence: mov byte ptr [edi+0x252], 1 at 0xAA0150 behind cmp byte [ebp+0xC], 0 at 0xAA0127 in CScrollbar_MoveBy; the two readers are recorded (LatchMoved 0x3F1320, AnySliderMoved 0x56480). Wrong if the struct the record calls CScrollbar were not the object MoveBy receives in EAX - it is, by MoveBy's own record.
